findings.title: New `upsampled_count()` aggregate is not marked private, bypassing the allowlist gate
findings.body: The new SnQLFunction `upsampled_count` (computing `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))`) is registered in the public function converter without `private=True`, unlike the function defined immediately above it which does set `private=True`. Because this function is publicly resolvable, any user/org can request it directly (e.g. `yAxis=upsampled_count()` or in `field`), completely bypassing the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` gate implemented in `error_upsampling.py`. For non-allowlisted projects where `sample_weight` is not meaningfully populated, this returns incorrect/misleading aggregate values, and more importantly it exposes an internal column (`sample_weight`) and computation path outside the intended governance of the feature flag/allowlist mechanism.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility check uses outer `dataset` instead of the `scoped_dataset` parameter actually being queried
findings.body: Inside `_get_event_stats(scoped_dataset, query_columns, query, snuba_params, ...)`, the call `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` references the enclosing `dataset` variable computed once in `get()`, not the `scoped_dataset` parameter that is actually used to execute the query (`scoped_dataset.run_top_events_timeseries_query`, `scoped_dataset.top_events_timeseries`, `scoped_dataset.timeseries_query`). In the dashboard-widget discover-split logic (`get_event_stats_factory`), `_get_event_stats` is invoked with varying first arguments (`discover`, `split_dataset`, `scoped_dataset`) that can differ from the outer `dataset`. As a result, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform` can make its decision based on the wrong dataset (e.g. outer dataset is `metrics_enhanced_performance` while the actual sub-query runs against `discover` with an error-focused query), causing upsampling to be incorrectly skipped or applied for that sub-query.

findings.title: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never called anywhere
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is documented as something that "should be called when the allowlist configuration changes to ensure cache consistency", but no code in this PR (or evidently elsewhere) calls it when the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option changes. This leaves the 60-second TTL as the only consistency mechanism, so removing a project from the allowlist (e.g. to fix an incident or stop a misconfiguration) will continue to serve stale, upsampled/scaled counts for up to 60 seconds with no way to force immediate invalidation, despite the function's docstring implying such a mechanism exists.

findings.title: Cache key derived from Python's built-in `hash()` on project id tuples risks collisions across different project sets
findings.body: `cache_key` is built as `f"error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))}"`. Using the generic `hash()` of a tuple (rather than a stable, collision-free encoding like a joined string of ids) means two different project-id sets within the same organization could theoretically hash-collide, causing the eligibility result computed for one project combination to be served for a different, unrelated combination for up to 60 seconds — i.e. a non-allowlisted project set could incorrectly inherit `True` (or vice versa), producing incorrect (scaled or unscaled) error counts for users.

findings.title: No fallback/null handling for `sample_weight`, risking silent undercount for pre-upsampling or non-sampled events
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites `count()` to `upsampled_count() as count` (i.e. `sum(sample_weight)`) for any allowlisted project, with the comment "no additional null checks are needed here" because sample_weight is assumed to exist for all events. If historical events ingested before this feature (or events not going through the client-sampling code path) have `sample_weight` as NULL or unset, `sum()` over those rows effectively treats them as 0 rather than 1, silently undercounting legitimate error events the moment a project is added to the allowlist, with no defensive `coalesce`/default applied in the SnQL (`sum(Column("sample_weight"))` in discover.py).

findings.title: Docstrings contradict each other regarding cache freshness
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` documents caching the allowlist eligibility result for 60 seconds ("Cache allowlist eligibility for 60 seconds ... eventual consistency is acceptable"), while the helper it calls on a cache miss, `_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, states "This function reads the allowlist configuration fresh each time... This is intentional to ensure we always have the latest configuration state." In practice, due to the 60-second cache wrapping it, the configuration is NOT read fresh on every call, contradicting the inner function's documented intent and potentially misleading future maintainers about the actual consistency guarantees.

findings.title: Unrelated/accidental file (looks like a git submodule reference) added to the PR
findings.body: The PR adds a file named `sentry-repo` whose only content is `Subproject commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`, which is characteristic of an accidentally committed git submodule/embedded repository reference rather than an intentional source change. This is unrelated to the stated feature, is not referenced by any other changed file, and risks causing checkout/tooling issues (e.g. "adding embedded git repository" warnings, or broken clones if the referenced commit isn't fetchable as a submodule) for anyone who clones or rebases on top of this commit. It should be removed before merge.

findings.title: No tests for the public caching entry point or cache invalidation
findings.body: The test suite only exercises private helpers (`_are_all_projects_error_upsampled`, `_is_error_focused_query`, `_should_apply_sample_weight_transform`, `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling`) but never calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` itself — the function that actually implements the caching behavior described as the PR's core "performance optimization". There is no test validating cache-hit vs cache-miss paths, TTL behavior, or that `invalidate_upsampling_cache` actually clears the correct key. Given the caching logic introduces real correctness risk (stale allowlist decisions, hash-based key collisions), this is the part of the change most in need of direct test coverage, and it currently has none.

findings.title: Broad silent exception swallowing in new test helper
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` wraps both the dict traversal (`normalized_data.get("contexts", {}).get("error_sampling", {}).get("client_sample_rate")`) and the float conversion in bare `except Exception: pass` blocks. Any malformed or unexpected shape of `contexts`/`error_sampling` (e.g. `contexts` explicitly set to `None`) will silently skip setting `sample_rate` with no logging or error surfaced, making it harder to diagnose why upsampling-related fixtures in tests produce unexpected counts if the test data doesn't match the expected shape exactly.
